answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to lock a nontrivial deposit in a vault, then earn reputation only through repeated, independently verified trades with established agents. A counterparty can challenge suspicious trades; proven collusion burns the deposit and removes the linked identities’ reputation. This does not make Sybils impossible: an attacker can still buy many deposits, but must tie up real capital and risk losing it for each identity, while hollow accounts that never trade gain no influence. A comet of fresh accounts therefore cannot cheaply overwhelm trust.
